title: Finite normalization models, semilinear functoriality and intermediate models
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $V$ an integral finite-type $k$-scheme, with function field $H=k(V)$. Let $M/H$ be a finite field extension and $N=\operatorname{Nor}_M(V)$ its normalization in $M$. Then $N$ is normal integral of finite type over $k$, its function field is canonically $M$, and $N\to V$ is finite surjective. Both $V$ and $N$ are Noetherian. If $V/k$ is separated, so is $N/k$. For every nonempty open $U\subseteq V$, the restriction $N_U$ is the normalization of $U$ in $M$. If $Z\to U$ is finite dominant, $Z$ is normal integral, and an $H$-embedding $k(Z)\hookrightarrow M$ is specified, there is exactly one $U$-morphism $N_U\to Z$ inducing this embedding, and that morphism is finite. For any two such data $(k,V,H,M)$ and $(k',V',H',M')$, an isomorphism of fields $k\cong k'$, a compatible semilinear scheme isomorphism $V\cong V'$, and a compatible field isomorphism $M\cong M'$ extending the induced isomorphism $H\cong H'$ induce a unique compatible isomorphism $N\cong N'$. These induced isomorphisms preserve identities and compositions. Thus every compatible group action on the scheme and field data extends uniquely to $N$, without any faithfulness or trivial-action-on-$k$ assumption.

Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain, and dominant means having dense image. The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally covered by spectra of Noetherian rings.

source.place: Tags 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain), 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize), 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective), together with the existing finite-normalization theorem lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite. Agent synthesis of affine normalization, semilinear transport and intermediate-model domination; de Jong §§3.2, 3.5 motivating models (local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: For every nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$, the germ embedding identifies $H$ with $\operatorname{Frac}A$. Put $C_A=\{x\in M:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }A\}$. By the definition of normalization, $N_W=\operatorname{Spec}C_A$. The integral-closure lemma gives that $C_A$ is a normal domain with fraction field canonically $M$. All these identifications use the given embedding $H\subset M$, so they agree on the generic field.

source.place: Tag 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal); affine normalization definition; finite-extension fraction-field clause of the cited node

proof.text: Each chart $\operatorname{Spec}C_A$ is integral, has generic point $(0)$ and function field $M$ by the spectrum/stalk lemma. Its local rings are localizations of $C_A$, hence normal domains by localization of normal domains. The chart generic points agree on overlaps: restricting to any nonempty affine open in the overlap of the base charts leaves the same embedding in $M$ and the same zero prime. Consequently there is one point dense in every chart and hence in $N$. The charts are reduced, so $N$ is reduced; the common dense point makes $N$ irreducible and nonempty. Thus $N$ is integral, normal, with the asserted canonical function field.

The existing finite-normalization theorem applies because $V$ is integral of finite type over the field $k$ and $M/H$ is finite. Thus $N\to V$ is finite, including for inseparable extensions. On each nonempty affine $W$, the inclusion $A\subset C_A$ is injective and integral by its construction. Lying over therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}C_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ surjective. These affine opens cover $V$, so $N\to V$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective); morphisms.tex Tag 0AVK (lemma-nagata-normalization-finite-general) specialized as lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover of $V$ by $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ finitely generated over $k$. Finiteness makes each inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ affine with $C_i$ a finite $A_i$-module. Generators of $A_i$ as a $k$-algebra together with generators of $C_i$ as an $A_i$-module generate $C_i$ as a $k$-algebra: every element is an $A_i$-linear combination of the latter generators. This finite affine cover proves $N/k$ is of finite type by the definition. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field; $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is also quasi-compact (one point). Applying finite-type-over-Noetherian to the two structure maps proves $V$ and $N$ Noetherian. When $V/k$ is separated, the finite-over-separated-finite-type lemma applied to $N\to V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ proves $N/k$ separated.

Let $U\subseteq V$ be nonempty open. Cover $U$ by nonempty affine opens. On each such $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, restriction of $N$ has coordinate ring precisely $C_A$ from step 1. These are the affine rings in the definition of the normalization of $U$ in $M$. On principal refinements the identification is the identity $x/s\mapsto x/s$ inside $M$, since integral closure commutes with localization; these identifications give the same gluing maps. Thus $N_U$ is canonically the normalization of $U$ in $M$. This argument does not require an intersection of two affine opens to be affine: cover the intersection by smaller affine opens.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); definition of normalization on arbitrary affine open covers

proof.text: Fix the intermediate-model data and write $j:k(Z)\hookrightarrow M$ for its specified $H$-embedding. For nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U$, finiteness gives $Z_W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite $A$-module. Dominance and integrality ensure this is a nonempty affine open of the integral scheme $Z$, so its germ map embeds $B$ in $k(Z)$. Every $b\in B$ is integral over $A$ by finite-algebra integrality. Applying $j$ to its monic equation shows $j(b)\in C_A$, because $j$ fixes $H$ and hence $A$. Thus $b\mapsto j(b)$ defines an $A$-algebra map $B\to C_A$, and the affine-spectrum correspondence gives an $W$-morphism $N_W\to Z_W$ inducing $j$ on generic fields.

source.place: Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral); affine spectrum correspondence and the monic-equation definition of integral closure

proof.text: The local maps of step 6 agree on overlaps. Indeed cover any overlap in $U$ by affine opens $W_0$; both restrictions are maps $N_{W_0}\to Z_{W_0}$ over $W_0$. Their coordinate maps become the same prescribed map $j$ in $M$; injectivity of the germ map of $N_{W_0}$ forces the coordinate maps equal. Scheme-morphism gluing therefore gives a unique map $N_U\to Z$ with these restrictions. The same test proves uniqueness among all $U$-maps inducing $j$. Finally, if $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ generate $C_A$ as an $A$-module, they generate it as a $B$-module via $B\to C_A$: the old expressions $c=\sum a_i c_i$ are also $B$-linear expressions. The inverse image of $Z_W$ is exactly $N_W$ since the map is over $U$. It is affine and finite on this affine cover of $Z$; since finiteness is local on the target (criterion (2) of the finite-local-on-target lemma, Stacks 01WI), the map is finite. Normality of $Z$ is an allowed hypothesis but is not needed for this construction.

source.place: schemes.tex Tag 01JA (glueing schemes); affine-spectrum correspondence and the definition of finite morphism

proof.text: For the semilinear clause write $f:V\xrightarrow{\sim}V'$. Use pullback direction for the supplied field isomorphism: let $\phi:M'\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ extend $f^*:H'\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ (invert the supplied forward isomorphisms if necessary). For affine $W'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset V'$, put $W=f^{-1}W'=\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $x'\in C_{A'}$ satisfies $(x')^n+\sum_{i<n}a_i'(x')^i=0$, then $\phi(x')^n+\sum_{i<n}f^*(a_i')\phi(x')^i=0$. Hence $\phi$ carries $C_{A'}$ into $C_A$. Applying the identical calculation to $\phi^{-1}$ proves equality and a ring isomorphism $C_{A'}\cong C_A$. Its spectrum is the desired local isomorphism over $f$, and on constants its pullback is the prescribed semilinear field map.

source.place: Agent monic-equation calculation using the affine normalization definition

proof.text: The local semilinear maps agree on overlaps by the same affine test as step 7: on any smaller affine base open both coordinate maps are restrictions of $\phi$ into $M$, and the target coordinate ring embeds in that field. Equivalently, on localized coordinates the formula is $x'/s'\mapsto\phi(x')/f^*(s')$, so all restriction maps commute. The gluing lemma gives a global map $F:N\to N'$ over $f$. Gluing the maps from $\phi^{-1}$ gives its inverse, since their composites on each chart are the identity ring homomorphism. Any compatible map has coordinate maps whose composites into $M$ equal $\phi$, so it has these same restrictions and equals $F$. Thus the global isomorphism is unique with the specified scheme and field data.

The lift of identity data is the identity, since it has those base and generic-field maps and step 9 gives uniqueness. For two composable data isomorphisms, the composite of their lifts has the composite base map and composite pullback on fields, so uniqueness identifies it with the lift of the composite. For a compatible left group action use the pullback of each geometric action map (equivalently the inverse of the corresponding left field automorphism). The lifted maps therefore satisfy $F_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $F_g\circ F_h=F_{gh}$. Every other compatible action has the same individual lifts by uniqueness. The coefficient field may move, and a group element acting trivially on both the scheme and field data lifts to the identity; no faithfulness or finiteness assumption on the group was used.

source.place: Agent identity/composition and group-law argument from the uniqueness established in step 9
